action_required: Reduce MYC (not MYCN or MYCL unless measured) activity or abundance, graded rather than total
cells: WWOX-deficient radial glia and early neurogenic progenitors in human organoids, isogenic corrected line as reference
window: during the radial-glia phase versus neuron-stage only (two arms), to separate a window; no claim that the window is prenatal only
expected_result: if MYC maintains the progenitor state: progenitor fraction and cycling fall towards the corrected line and neuron markers (NEUN, CTIP2, SATB2, absolute counts per organoid) rise without loss of the SOX2+ pool
outcome_showing_hypothesis_wrong: Wrong if: markers do not move at matched MYC lowering; absolute SOX2+ pool shrinks or glia rise (fate shift); death rises; or the same lowering in corrected organoids produces the same shift (then it is generic acceleration, not repair); MYCN rises to compensate Note: the published A51 experiment has no wild-type plus tool arm (E83), so the corrected-line control has no precedent in the source.
missing_premise: MYC amount or activity per cell in radial glia (protein is measured as a SOX2+MYC+ fraction and by immunoblot in 2D NSCs, but not per cell), MYC in a corrected or rescued arm, and any MYCN or MYCL comparison are unmeasured; MYC binding at neuronal genes is lost in knockout NSCs with MYC protein high (E80), so a gain of MYC activity is not shown.
tools_or_compounds_identity_action_conte: EN4 (covalent ligand of MYC cysteine 171; Boike 2020, PMID 32966806, found by the auditor): used at 50 uM, the maximum of its discovery paper (solubility limit), continuous exposure, one donor line in the other-disease model; C171 is not conserved in MYCN or MYCL (selectivity suggested, untested); eight other off-targets seen; not used in WWOX models. 10074-G5, a MYC/MAX dimerisation inhibitor, did not meet the abundance criterion there (not 'failed': it was not expected to lower abundance). Genetic lowering is the first tool.
compound_justified: not justified as a name; genetic lowering is the justified first tool
discriminating_experiment: three-arm organoid design: shRNA or inducible degron to MYC at graded levels, against scrambled, in knockout, SCAR12-class and corrected lines; absolute cell counts; MYC, MYCN, MYCL measured in the same cells
status: conditional: missing premise is MYC protein elevation in radial glia and tolerance of lowering

action_required: Restore cell-cycle timing (lengthen G1 or slow S and G2M) without changing MYC
expected_result: if the cell-cycle shift is the cause of the maturation delay: neuron markers rise with MYC still high; if MYC is the maintainer: no rescue
outcome_showing_hypothesis_wrong: Wrong if: neuron markers do not move while cycling falls, or MYC falls on its own (then the cycle shift was upstream of MYC); or the pool collapses
missing_premise: whether the cell-cycle shift is robust: the single-cell density curves are near-superimposed, but the same paper has an orthogonal protein readout (pH3+ SOX2+ fraction raised in knockout and WOREE-class, Supp 6A-B) and the S fraction is up about 1.7-fold (Fig 4C); and whether a G1-lengthening perturbation is tolerated by these cells; the nocodazole result in the other-disease model is not a precedent (microtubule poison, E27).
tools_or_compounds_identity_action_conte: no compound named: the only G1 perturbation read shortens G1 (cyclin D1 and E1 forcing) in mouse and cannot be read as the opposite; an antimitotic arrest (mitotic block) did not rescue in the other-disease model
discriminating_experiment: discriminating experiment only: genetic G1 lengthening (for instance a CDK inhibitor gene) against genetic MYC lowering, factorial, in the same organoid batch; measure MYC, phase, markers and counts
status: conditional: missing premise is the size and reality of the cell-cycle shift
